claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength, in part because it contains the hard B2 phase.
Stress concentrations at the incoherent phase interfaces cause brittleness and interfacial cracking.
Applying 6 GPa at 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the FCC/B2 lamellae into a hierarchical patterned microstructure.
The HPHT-induced hierarchical microstructure will have coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Coherent interfaces can permit dislocations or partial dislocations to transfer across a boundary.
Dislocation transfer across coherent FCC/B2 interfaces will alleviate interfacial stress concentrations.
The coherent hierarchical structure will promote dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning.
The activated deformation mechanisms will produce a more homogeneous strain distribution between the FCC and B2 phases.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
The proposed structure and deformation mechanisms will arrest interfacial cracking.
HPHT treatment will enhance ductility without sacrificing strength.
The HPHT-treated sample will exhibit elongated cracks rather than isolated microcracks on its fracture surface.
The untreated alloy exhibits isolated microcracks and divergent phase-specific GND densities.
Pressure and temperature must be high enough to cause the proposed topology and coherence change but below conditions causing phase instability or melting.
Conventional annealing or rolling will not produce equivalent hierarchical interface coherence, GND homogenization, and fracture morphology.
Coherent nanotwin or nanoprecipitate interfaces in other material systems can support dislocation-mediated deformation or strengthening.
The exact pressure-temperature window for obtaining coherent FCC/B2 interfaces without phase decomposition is uncertain.
